A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MGSR study, with readable and matchable text, equations, seven figures, and four tables. Neither supplied PDF contains appendix pages, despite both referring to an Appendix; the assessment covers the supplied contents.

before.justification: v1 reports original rendering and reconstruction experiments, quantitative comparisons in Tables 1–3, qualitative results, and ablations in Table 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results and ablations in Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–7.

M1.justification: The two branches, illumination decomposition, losses, alternating supervision, auto-stop strategy, and mesh extraction remain unchanged. The explanation after Equation (15) corrects references to already-defined losses; it does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same rendering and reconstruction tasks using DTU, OmniObject3D, Shiny Blender, Ref-NeRF Real Captured Scenes, and Tanks and Temples. The represented objects and illustrated scenes are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains 3D-GS, GS-IR, GShader, and R3DG. Table 2 retains NeuS2, 2D-GS, and GOF; Table 3 and the corresponding visual comparisons retain 2D-GS and GOF.

E3.justification: The reported protocol retains 15 DTU scans, three Shiny Blender objects, 30 OmniObject3D objects, 10K sampled reconstruction points, and the same metrics. Table 2's exclusion of failed objects and Table 4's optimization settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 4 retains all A–M configurations testing branch weights, depth-loss weight, optimization duration, bidirectional back-propagation, and auto-stop warm-up. The geometry demonstration and qualitative case comparisons also remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither supplied version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 match, including baseline results and runtimes. For example, MGSR's Shiny Blender and OmniObject3D PSNR values remain 34.66 and 37.69. The qualitative comparisons and reported ablation findings are also retained.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(15) retain their substance. Equation (10) adopts double-bar norm notation, and Equation (15)'s explanatory references are corrected; neither introduces new mathematics, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: jointly improving rendering and reconstruction through mutually supervising 2D/3D Gaussian branches, geometry-guided illumination decomposition, and auto-stop warm-up.

C2.justification: The interpretations of geometry guidance, normal consistency, and branch supervision remain intact. Both versions acknowledge low-light oversmoothing and lost detail and propose exposure compensation as future work; v2 rephrases this discussion more tentatively.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository address in the abstract. Its new acknowledgment identifies Fudan University's CFFF platform as the computational resource. These are additional disclosures, not evidence of changed experiments.

R1.justification: The same 29 cited works and research-positioning arguments remain. Reference reordering and publication-detail updates, including PGSR and the Gaussian-splatting survey, do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammatical edits, standardizes 2DGS/3DGS terminology, corrects the loss cross-references, consolidates author information, and adds acknowledgments. The section sequence and most prose remain intact; the limitations paragraph is reworded.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from a single-column preprint layout to two columns, with redesigned front matter and relocated or resized figures and tables. The visual evidence is retained, but Table 2 becomes substantially smaller. Table 4's weight label is aligned with the equation notation.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves technical clarity and reproducibility guidance by correcting the loss references after Equation (15), adding code-access information, and identifying the computing platform. The scientific evidence remains unchanged. The smaller Table 2 reduces readability, limiting the benefit of the revision, but the documentation corrections support a modest net improvement.
